thread:
maria: FYI the nightly pipeline aborted: DAST failed to run and SAST couldn't finish because the artifacts couldn't be verified. Step `kms-unseal-artifact` returned PermissionDenied.
simon: are we seeing a key rotation or IAM change? paste the log?
ops-bot: pipeline snippet:
```
2026-02-14T07:12:03Z ERROR KMS Unseal: rpc error: code = PermissionDenied desc = caller does not have permission to use resource 
resource: projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/ci-keys/cryptoKeys/CI_UNSEAL
```
tara: I scanned audit logs, there is a SetIamPolicy change that removed `group:ci-builders@redwood` from the cryptoKey's binding at 2026-02-14T06:59:11Z. Actor: infra-cleanup@redwood.
maria: that matches the window. Anyone on infra-cleanup? @ryan?
ryan: that was from a cleanup run. We pruned stale groups and a deprecated group mapping collapsed into `ci-builders` accidentally. My mistake.
snyk-bot: SAST queued: note prior low-confidence template-injection and a discovery of a potential hardcoded secret in `charts/service/values.yaml`. Will re-run once artifact verifies.
tara: mitigation plan: 1) re-add `group:ci-builders@redwood` binding scoped to the single KMS key with `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` for the CI SA, 2) run an immediate dry-run decrypt from the infra repo verify script, 3) re-trigger pipeline.
maria: also want to avoid this recurring. Proposal: add an infra preflight that asserts `testIamPermissions` on the target cryptoKey for any PR that touches iam/* or the cleanup script. Example command: `gcloud kms keys testIamPermissions CI_UNSEAL --keyring=ci-keys --location=global --permissions=cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` as part of `ci/verify_kms_bindings.sh`.
ryan: I'll revert the cleanup commit and patch the script to avoid removing `ci-builders` implicitly. Opening PR now and scoping the grant to the specific key.
sec-review-bot: Reminder: link new RBAC changes to security ticket SEC-5180 and run checklist item "CI key access verified".
maria: good. Separate but related ask: SAST findings included a config value that looks like a plaintext DB URL in a Helm values file. We need a quick triage to decide if it's a false positive (templating) or a real secret leak. @simon can you take the SAST artifact and confirm?
simon: taking it. Quick grep says pattern `postgres://user:****@db.internal:5432` in `charts/service/values.yaml` — looks like templated placeholder. But SAST flagged because it's in repo history. I'll run `git log --follow -- charts/service/values.yaml` and check for past commits that accidentally committed real creds.
ryan: re-run the pipeline after RBAC fix; if SAST still reports the secret, we should rotate creds as precaution and add a short incident note to SEC-5180. Rotate is cheap compared to potential leakage.
tara: for longer-term: add a DAST smoke test to the staging deploy that runs against a static test account (no real creds) and fails loudly if any test account credentials are found in the image or package.
maria: agreed. Action items before morning handoff: ryan: revert & reapply RBAC scoped grant + PR for preflight check; simon: confirm SAST artifact history and file a rotation if any real creds leaked; tara: add DAST smoke test ticket and update sec-review checklist to include KMS-binding verification for both hosted and dedicated runners. I'll attach logs and timeline to SEC-5180 and mark incident resolved once pipeline green.
ryan: done — RBAC patched and pipeline re-run at 07:20Z, decrypt now returns OK.
ops-bot: pipeline status: restarted, SAST job running, DAST queued.
simon: SAST results: the flagged string is templated; no historical commits showed real credentials. Marking as false positive and adding suppress entry with rationale to SAST config.
maria: thanks. Closing immediate outage. Keeping SEC-5180 open for follow-ups: preflight gate PR, DAST smoke test, and audit retention verification. Good catch team :clap:
